name: MA-09
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+6 Massachusetts district with incumbent Bill Keating seeking reelection
Keating holds roughly a ten-to-one cash-on-hand advantage over MacAllister
Polymarket prices Keating near 96% to win
No public polling or expert ratings; outlook rests on fundamentals
model.rationale: The district's Democratic lean, Keating's incumbency, and a tenfold cash advantage over MacAllister all point to a comfortable win, and prediction markets price Keating as near certain. With no polling available, the forecast stays close to fundamentals and expects a margin in the high teens.
model.watch: Fresh polling showing a tighter race or a late influx of outside spending for MacAllister would be the first sign of movement.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Massachusetts' 9th District leans Democratic, and incumbent Bill Keating is seeking another term with the advantages that come with it. He has raised more than $530,000 and holds over $510,000 on hand, roughly ten times the cash of Republican Tyler MacAllister. No public polls cover the race and no expert raters have weighed in, so the outlook rests on fundamentals and market pricing.

Prediction markets put Keating's chances around 96%, consistent with a comfortable win in a district that favored Democrats by six points at the presidential level. MacAllister has run a credible fundraising effort for a challenger but lacks the resources to close the gap quickly. The forecast expects Keating to win by a wide margin, with the main uncertainty coming from the absence of polling rather than any specific sign of vulnerability.
